title: Unità 3 · Amici e famiglia
question: Who is in my family, and what do we want or have to do?
workingOn: family words, my / your, and voglio, devo, posso
canDo: I can refer to family members using possessives.
I can read and interpret a story related to family members.
I can describe and talk about family lineage.
I can talk about wants and obligations.
culture: In Italy, grandparents (i nonni) often help raise their grandchildren: they pick them up from school and cook for them. Many families still meet for a long Sunday lunch, often at the grandparents' house. Many young Italians live with their parents until their late twenties or longer.

grammar.head: my / your match the noun: mio padre, mia madre · voglio, devo, posso + a verb: Devo studiare.
tricks: One family member = no article: mia madre, tuo fratello. More than one keeps it: i miei nonni.
Mamma, papà, and pets keep the article: la mia mamma, il mio papà, il mio cane.
The possessive matches the thing, not the owner: Marco e sua sorella.
After voglio, devo, posso, use the whole verb: Voglio giocare. Devo studiare. Posso uscire?

sentences: I miei nonni sono di Napoli.
Can I go out with my friends?
We have to eat with our grandparents.

forms.why: madre is feminine and one person: mia, no article.
padre is masculine and one person: mio, no article.
Plural family words keep the article: i miei nonni.
trick: i miei nonni, i miei genitori.

forms.why: sorella is feminine, one person: tua, no article.
A pet is not family: keep the article. il mio cane.
trick: il mio cane, il mio gatto.

forms.why: sorella is feminine → sua, even though Marco is a boy.
trick: match the thing, not the owner
Marco e sua sorella. Anna e suo fratello.
Voglio giocare = I want to play.
Deve studiare = he has to study.
Puoi uscire? = Can you go out?

fill.hint: my (madre is feminine) → starts with M-i-a.
fill.why: One family member, feminine: Mia madre, no article.
nonni is masculine plural: i miei nonni.
cane is masculine singular: il mio cane.
One family member, masculine: tuo fratello, no article.

fill.hint: you have to → starts with d-e-v, ends in -i.
she wants → starts with v-u, ends in -e.

read.title: La famiglia di Sofia
passage: Ciao, sono Sofia. Ho due fratelli e un cane.
Hi, I'm Sofia. I have two brothers and a dog.
Mia nonna è di Napoli ed è molto simpatica.
My grandmother is from Naples and she's very nice.
Il pranzo della domenica è a casa della nonna.
Sunday lunch is at Grandma's house.
Oggi non posso uscire: devo studiare!
Today I can't go out: I have to study!

questions.why: Il pranzo della domenica è a casa della nonna.
Oggi non posso uscire: devo studiare!

listen.en: How many brothers do you have?
Do you want to play or study?

lines: Hi Anna! Can you go out today?
No, non posso. Devo mangiare con i nonni.
No, I can't. I have to eat with my grandparents.
Sì! E dopo mio nonno vuole giocare a carte. 🃏
Yes! And after, my grandpa wants to play cards.
Anche lui! Tale padre, tale figlio! 😄
Him too! Like father, like son!

prompts: No, non posso. Devo … / Sì, posso!
checks: Ho detto una cosa del mio compagno.

finish: Now I know how to talk about my family and say what I want, have to, and can do!

idiom.ex: Marco è alto e simpatico come suo padre. Tale padre, tale figlio!
idiom.exEn: Marco is tall and nice like his father. Like father, like son!
idiom.note: Said when a child looks or acts just like a parent, the same as the English saying.

flags: Infinitives after the modals (mangiare, studiare, giocare, uscire) are taught as memorized chunks; regular conjugation is not taught yet.
Possible duplication: the existing Italiano 1 game already has a 'Volere, dovere, potere' unit and 'Unità 2 · -are e voglio, devo, posso'. Decide whether this unit replaces or reviews it.
Possessives cover mio, tuo, suo, nostro only (vocab cap). vostro and il loro are not taught here; add them if your guide expects all six.
Trick: la mia mamma / il mio papà keep the article. This is standard usage but some teachers teach mia mamma as also acceptable in speech; confirm your preference.
Reading uses della in 'Il pranzo della domenica' and 'a casa della nonna' (articulated preposition, not taught yet); both are glossed as chunks.
Chunks used without a taught chart: oggi, dopo, molto, Anche lui, giocare a carte, Quanti…? (all glossed or assumed known from Unit 1).
Sentence 12 'Dobbiamo mangiare con i nonni' translates i nonni as 'our grandparents' (natural Italian drops the possessive here). Fine for students, but worth a word in class.
Culture facts are unverified (general trends; vary by region and family).
